messages.subject: markerlrt()
parts:
Hi ,

segregation distortion is high in my dataset so I have decided to try markerlrt() along with est.rf()

 

when I run:

All_q50C50LRT <- markerlrt(All_q50C50)

and use:

lod <- formLinkageGroups(All_q50C50LRT, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=8)

[I’ve tried a range of max.rf and min.lod values]

the result is always 1 marker per linkage group

 

what have I done wrong?

thanks, roberta

Maybe the markers aren't coming out as linked?
Try making a histogram of the LOD scores.

Use something like this:

data(hyper)
hyper <- markerlrt(hyper)
lod <- pull.rf(hyper, what="lod")
hist(lod, breaks=100)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] markerlrt()
parts:
using All_q50C50LRT <- markerlrt(All_q50C50)

the histogram distribution is right-skewed with lod 1 = 1750000, lod 2 =2500000, lod 3 = 1250000, lod 4 = 750000, lod 5 = 250000 and then drops pretty sharply with no visible tail past LOD 10 scale bar

 

with All_q50C50EST <- est.rf(All_q50C50)

I get a similar distribution, lod 2 =2500000, lod 3 = 1250000, lod 4 = 750000, lod 5 = 250000

but lod 1 <250000, and the drop is more gradual with visible tail past LOD 30 scale bar

 

I did recover linkage among HWE markers using est.rf

~900 markers are assigned to the first 9 linkage groups

based on earlier work, I am able to assign 8 linkage groups to chromosomes

I am interested in using lrt because  I want to include nonHWE markers in the map

thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] markerlrt()
parts:
Sorry it's taken me so long to figure this out...

It seems that if you use markerlrt() in place of est.rf(), you need to use max.rf=Inf when you call formLinkagegroups:

All_q50C50LRT <- markerlrt(All_q50C50)
lg <- formLinkageGroups(All_q50C50LRT, max.rf=Inf, min.lod=10)

I'll fix this in the next release.

karl
